sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Westonka High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Westonka High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Westonka High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cornersville High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Cornersville High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Cornersville High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Fort Dale Academy Greenville Al basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Fort Dale Academy Greenville Al basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Fort Dale Academy Greenville Al basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Westfield Technical Academy Westfield Ma basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Westfield Technical Academy Westfield Ma basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Pinecrest Academy Of Nevada Sloan Canyon basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Pinecrest Academy Of Nevada Sloan Canyon basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Pinecrest Academy Of Nevada Sloan Canyon basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Fayetteville Manlius High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Fayetteville Manlius High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Fayetteville Manlius High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Gannon University Athletics basketball highlight
sections.text: For a personal college basketball highlight, keep the build-up to the shot in view. Start before the catch or final dribble and end after the ball reaches the hoop. Add the tracer to make the flight visible while preserving the pace and context of the possession.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Gannon University Athletics basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Sumner Academy Kansas basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Sumner Academy Kansas basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Sumner Academy Kansas basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Riverfield Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Riverfield Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Riverfield Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Elm Grove Middle School basketball clip

sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Elm Grove Middle School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Elm Grove Middle School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Elm Grove Middle School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Sports And Medical Sciences Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Sports And Medical Sciences Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Sports And Medical Sciences Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Flint Cultural Center Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Flint Cultural Center Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Flint Cultural Center Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Young Men'S Leadership Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Young Men'S Leadership Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Young Men'S Leadership Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Young Men'S Leadership Academy basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
Can I use a basketball practice clip?
Yes. A single practice attempt with a visible release, ball flight and basket is a useful starting point. Keep the camera steady and leave enough space in frame for the full shot.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.
Is the demo a Young Men'S Leadership Academy basketball video?
The demo is a shared HoopCut basketball example. It lets you see the effect before uploading your own clip. HoopCut is an independent editing tool.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Southside School Batesville Ar basketball highlight

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence

subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Althoff Catholic High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Althoff Catholic High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Forest Hills High School Nc basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Forest Hills High School Nc basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Forest Hills High School Nc basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your The North Carolina Leadership Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for The North Carolina Leadership Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your The North Carolina Leadership Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Avon Middle School South basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Avon Middle School South basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Avon Middle School South basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Fayette Academy Somerville basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Fayette Academy Somerville basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Fayette Academy Somerville basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

heading: Frankton High School basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Have a basketball clip from Frankton High School? Make the shot stand out with a visible ball trail. Upload your recording, select the play and preview your traced highlight — from the catch to the finish at the basket.
heroDetail: Keep the pass, release and finish in view. Select up to 30 seconds, mark the hoop and preview the effect before saving your clip.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Frankton High School basketball clip
workflowHeading: From game recording to traced basketball highlight
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Frankton High School basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Frankton High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Frankton High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Frankton High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Faith Academy Bellville basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Faith Academy Bellville basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Faith Academy Bellville basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cpa Academy Nashville basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Cpa Academy Nashville basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Cpa Academy Nashville basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Twin Cities Academy Mn basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Twin Cities Academy Mn basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Twin Cities Academy Mn basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your North Stanly High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for North Stanly High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your North Stanly High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

heroDetail: Start with one clear attempt: the shooter, ball and basket in frame. Select up to 30 seconds and preview the trail before exporting.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Erie First Christian Academy basketball clip

sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Erie First Christian Academy basketball highlights

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Erie First Christian Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Erie First Christian Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Erie First Christian Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Southampton Academy Courtland Va basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Southampton Academy Courtland Va basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Southampton Academy Courtland Va basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Lourdes Academy Oshkosh basketball

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Western Beaver High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Western Beaver High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Memphis Academy Of Science And Engineering basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Memphis Academy Of Science And Engineering basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Memphis Academy Of Science And Engineering basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Maine Farmington University basketball highlight

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Maine Farmington University basketball

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your East Coast Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for East Coast Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your East Coast Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Newark Collegiate Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Newark Collegiate Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Newark Collegiate Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Moffat County High School basketball

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Moffat County High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Cesar Chavez Academy High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Cesar Chavez Academy High School basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Cesar Chavez Academy High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Purnell Swett High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Legacy Prep The Woodlands basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Legacy Prep The Woodlands basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Legacy Prep The Woodlands basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.

toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Bloom Carroll High School basketball clip
