sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Bloom Carroll High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Bloom Carroll High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Bloom Carroll High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Foxboro High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Foxboro High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Erie First Christian Academy Erie Pa basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Erie First Christian Academy Erie Pa basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Erie First Christian Academy Erie Pa basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Kirbyville High School basketball clip

sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Kirbyville High School basketball highlights

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Kirbyville High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Kirbyville High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Kirbyville High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

description: Add a shot tracer to your own Brownsburg West Middle School basketball clip. Upload a game recording, preview the ball trail and export your highlight.
heading: Brownsburg West Middle School basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Have a basketball clip from Brownsburg West Middle School? Make the shot stand out with a visible ball trail. Upload your recording, select the play and preview your traced highlight — from the catch to the finish at the basket.
heroDetail: Keep the pass, release and finish in view. Select up to 30 seconds, mark the hoop and preview the effect before saving your clip.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Brownsburg West Middle School basketball clip
workflowHeading: From game recording to traced basketball highlight
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Brownsburg West Middle School basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Brownsburg West Middle School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Brownsburg West Middle School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Brownsburg West Middle School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Meeker High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Meeker High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Meeker High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Provision Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Provision Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Provision Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Riverside High School Yonkers basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Riverside High School Yonkers basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Riverside High School Yonkers basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

description: Make your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball shot stand out. Upload a practice or game clip, preview a tracer and export a highlight with HoopCut.
heading: Hackett Catholic Prep basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Turn your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball recording into a highlight worth sharing. Pick a jumper from practice or a game, upload your clip and add a visible trail that follows the ball toward the hoop.
heroDetail: Start with one clear attempt: the shooter, ball and basket in frame. Select up to 30 seconds and preview the trail before exporting.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball clip
workflowHeading: From practice recording to a shareable shot
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Hackett Catholic Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Hackett Catholic Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Warren Academy basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Warren Academy basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Warren Academy basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Johnson & Wales University Sports basketball highlight
sections.text: For a personal college basketball highlight, keep the build-up to the shot in view. Start before the catch or final dribble and end after the ball reaches the hoop. Add the tracer to make the flight visible while preserving the pace and context of the possession.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Johnson & Wales University Sports basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Naval Academy Rhode Island basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Naval Academy Rhode Island basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Naval Academy Rhode Island basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Trinity Christian Academy Addison Tx basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Trinity Christian Academy Addison Tx basketball

subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

heading: Capital City High School basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Have a basketball clip from Capital City High School? Make the shot stand out with a visible ball trail. Upload your recording, select the play and preview your traced highlight — from the catch to the finish at the basket.
heroDetail: Keep the pass, release and finish in view. Select up to 30 seconds, mark the hoop and preview the effect before saving your clip.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Capital City High School basketball clip
workflowHeading: From game recording to traced basketball highlight
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Capital City High School basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Capital City High School basketball highlight
sections.text: A useful game highlight shows how the shot develops. Start just before the catch or dribble, keep the release in view and let the clip run until the ball reaches the basket. A tracer draws attention to the flight, while the surrounding play gives viewers the moment that led to it.

subsections.heading: Keep the setup and finish together
subsections.text: For a catch-and-shoot play, include the pass. For a pull-up jumper, include the last dribble. Trim dead time around the possession so the highlight stays focused on the shot.

sections.heading: A game clip plan for Capital City High School basketball
sections.text: Find the possession in your recording and note its timestamp. Include the pass or last dribble, the release and the finish. Use that continuous section in the uploader, then watch the tracer at both ends of the shot before saving.

subsections.heading: When to choose a different possession
subsections.text: A crowded lane, a sudden zoom or a camera pan can hide the ball. Preview the full shot and choose a clearer recording if the trail does not follow the visible flight.

sections.heading: Preview the tracer through a busy game sequence
sections.text: Upload your saved clip in the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Watch the preview from release to finish. Pay particular attention when a defender crosses the ball or the camera pans: the finished trail should help viewers follow the shot.

subsections.heading: Check the moment the ball leaves the hand
subsections.text: Replay the release and the arrival at the rim. If the ball disappears behind another player, try a clearer attempt from your recording and compare the result.

sections.heading: Save your Capital City High School basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: When the preview looks right, export the Firework effect free and save the traced version alongside your original. Give the file a useful name with the game date and play so you can find it when putting together a personal highlight collection.

subsections.heading: Prepare the clip for sharing
subsections.text: Play the saved clip once before sharing it. Include the player or game details you know in your caption, and retain the source recording if you want a longer version later.

faq: How do I add a tracer to my Capital City High School basketball video?
Upload your saved recording using the tool above, select up to 30 seconds and mark the hoop. Preview the shot trail, then export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the result.
What makes a game clip suitable for a shot tracer?

Choose a continuous shot with the ball and basket visible. Include the pass or final dribble, the release and the finish. If players block the ball, inspect the preview carefully or choose a clearer attempt.
Can I paste a Hudl link into this uploader?
Use a video file saved on your device. This uploader does not import Hudl links; upload a recording you own or have permission to edit.
Is the demo a Capital City High School basketball video?
The demo is a shared HoopCut basketball example. It lets you see the effect before uploading your own clip. HoopCut is an independent editing tool.

heading: Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball highlights — add a shot tracer
intro: Turn your Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball recording into a highlight worth sharing. Pick a jumper from practice or a game, upload your clip and add a visible trail that follows the ball toward the hoop.
heroDetail: Start with one clear attempt: the shooter, ball and basket in frame. Select up to 30 seconds and preview the trail before exporting.
toolHeading: Add a tracer to your Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball clip
workflowHeading: From practice recording to a shareable shot
sampleHeading: See how a shot tracer changes a basketball clip
faqHeading: Editing your Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball highlights
examplesHeading: Watch the ball trail in action

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Yes Prep Southwest Secondary basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.

sections.heading: Choose a shot for your Creighton Prep basketball highlight
sections.text: A practice jumper can make a clear, focused highlight. Choose an attempt where the ball stays visible from release to basket, with a little time before and after the shot. Use the tracer to draw attention to the flight without cutting away the footwork and follow-through.

subsections.heading: Start with one uninterrupted attempt
subsections.text: Pick a continuous section of the recording rather than a montage with cuts during the shot. Keep the phone steady and leave room above the shooter for the full arc.

sections.heading: A practice clip plan for Creighton Prep basketball
sections.text: Before recording, frame the shooter and basket together. Leave space above the rim for the arc, record one complete attempt and keep the camera steady through the follow-through. In the editor, select that attempt and review the trail before export.

subsections.heading: What to keep in the frame
subsections.text: Keep the ball visible at release and on its approach to the rim. If a wall, another player or the camera crop hides part of the flight, choose a clearer take.

sections.heading: Make the shot trail easy to follow
sections.text: Upload the recording, select the attempt and mark the basket. Preview the trail against the gym or outdoor background. Check that you can still see the ball and follow its path all the way toward the hoop before choosing your finished version.

subsections.heading: Review the clip at its original framing
subsections.text: Make sure the basket and the top of the shot remain in frame. A tight crop that cuts off part of the arc makes the effect harder to follow.

sections.heading: Save your Creighton Prep basketball clip with a tracer
sections.text: Export the Firework effect free when you are happy with the preview. Keep the edited attempt beside the original practice recording and give it a session date or shot label so it is easy to find when you want to share it.

subsections.heading: Keep a copy for your next practice review
subsections.text: Save the original as well as the traced copy. The trail is a visual effect that makes a shot easier to follow; it does not measure shooting accuracy or release mechanics.
